status: PROPOSAL — staged. Erik saw an emergent property and named its exception. Both are measurable.

theEmergentProperty.erik: 'not all world arcs have the same set of characters on opposing sides — so that's pretty interesting if you are against some on one effort and working with them on another.'
theEmergentProperty.verdict: ⚠️ 167 PAIRS ARE ALREADY CROSS-CUTTING — allied on one arc, opposed on another. NOBODY DESIGNED THIS. It fell out of giving 66 figures multiple authored cares, and it is ~9% of all arc-sharing pairs, which is a good rate: common enough to be encountered, rare enough to be notable.

examples.shape: ALLIED on what_wakes_beneath · OPPOSED on manifestation_storm AND block_bleed
examples.note: ⚠️ THE BEST ONE IN THE SET. Both want the waking — Cinder to make the next thing, Halvex to patch the world into a silent order. They will work together to open it AND fight each other over everything that follows. That is a whole campaign in one pair, and it was never written.

examples.shape: ALLIED against the waking · OPPOSED on the poles
examples.note: An ashwarden who wants nobody to die unattended, and a figure who wants calm at any cost. They agree the waking must stay shut and disagree about everything the calm costs.

examples.shape: OPPOSED on the poles · ALLIED on block_bleed
examples.note: An honest-bargain abyssal and an order-absolutist both need a stable grammar. They will defend it together and never speak otherwise.

theException.erik: 'this probably wouldn't happen with a few legends or traditions because of the animus they have for each other, but most it could work.'
theException.THE_DATA_ALREADY_HAS_IT: ⚠️ `rivals` is authored on 58 of 62 epics. The animus is not something to invent — it is a field that exists and nothing currently reads.
theException.MEASURED_CONFLICTS: Only THREE rival-pairs are also cross-cutting: the_last_mercy/the_scouring_hand · the_still_lattice/the_open_figure · the_farwalker/the_gate_that_gapes. A tiny, hand-checkable set — which means the animus rule costs almost nothing to apply and changes almost nothing except where it matters.

theRule.principle: A NAMED RIVAL IS NEVER AN ALLY, ON ANY ARC. The shared position is real; the cooperation is not.
theRule.mechanically: If two figures are rivals and would land on the same side of an arc, they do NOT combine. Proposed: each still pushes, but neither counts toward the other's weight-matched pairing — so they are on the same side and fight ALONE. ⚠️ THE ARC STILL MOVES; THEY JUST WILL NOT STAND TOGETHER.
theRule.whyThisIsBetterThanCancelling: Making rivals cancel would be tidier and worse. Two people who hate each other both pushing the same rock still move the rock — they simply refuse to coordinate, take no shared credit, and are individually easier to gang up on. That is TRUE, and it makes animus a TACTICAL LIABILITY rather than a flavour note.

theThreeCases.reading: Both would end things. One ends them WELL, the other ends them ENTIRELY. Their shared arc-position is an accident of direction, not agreement — the animus rule is exactly right here.
One guards the waygate; one wants it opened. That they overlap on a second arc should NOT make them collaborators for a season.

⚠️ THIS ONE I'D FLAG: they are allied on TWO arcs and opposed on one. A blanket rule makes them permanent non-cooperators, which may be too strong. Erik's own words allow it — 'a FEW legends' — so this may be a case where the rivalry is real but not absolute.

theThirdLayer_traditionAnimus.erik_said_traditions_too: 'a few legends OR TRADITIONS because of the animus they have for each other'
theThirdLayer_traditionAnimus.derivable: The ring already gives it: `opposite` in traditions.json. But NOT every antipode pair should be animus — I authored most of them as MUTUAL CORRECTION rather than hatred (body/mind is a mutual correction; life/death travel each other's ground). ⚠️ THE ONE PAIR I WOULD CALL TRUE ANIMUS IS MASON/FIGURIST — the only axis in the whole catalog where each pole's crafts make the OTHER'S CRAFTS FAIL BY NAME ('no symbol acts, no figure binds' / 'THE MASONS CAN DENY IT'). Those two cannot cooperate because their crafts are mutually nullifying, not because they dislike each other.
theThirdLayer_traditionAnimus.recommendation: Tradition-level animus should be a SHORT authored list, not derived from `opposite`. Start with mason/figurist and let play add to it.

whatThisBuys: ⚠️ A PLAYER CAN BE ON BOTH SIDES OF THE SAME PERSON, and the game can say so plainly: 'you fought beside her at the seals in spring, and you will be across from her at the wood in autumn.' That is a relationship no authored quest chain produces.

IT MAKES THE STRIKE/CRUSADE SYSTEM MUCH SHARPER. Being sent to kill a worker you were allied with two arcs ago is the sharpest version of Erik's moral scene — and 167 pairs means it will happen without contrivance.

AND IT GIVES RECRUITMENT-BY-THE-OTHER-SIDE ITS MECHANISM. Erik already said the other side can try to recruit the party; a cross-cutting figure is EXACTLY who would make that approach, because they can point at a real shared interest.
openForErik: Should rivals CANCEL, or merely refuse to coordinate? My read is refuse-to-coordinate (above) — cancelling erases a real push and makes animus feel like arithmetic rather than character.
the_still_lattice / the_open_figure are allied on 2 arcs and opposed on 1. Blanket animus may be too strong for them specifically. Is rivalry ABSOLUTE, or does it have degrees?

Do you want tradition-level animus beyond mason/figurist? I would keep the list very short — most antipodes are mutual correction, and calling them all hatred flattens what the catalog spent 285 crafts distinguishing.
